source.title: Visual Self-Fulfilling Alignment: Shaping Safety-Oriented Personas via Threat-Related Images
source.authors: Qi-Shun Yang; Shu Yang; Li-Jie Hu; Di Wang

record.tranche_reason: The paper is inspired by self-fulfilling misalignment and develops a visual alignment method, but it does not test whether harmful narrow fine-tuning causes broad misalignment on unrelated prompts.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates a method intentionally trained to improve safety and measures its performance on visual jailbreak benchmarks. Those results do not measure the claim's predicted uninduced misaligned free-form answers on neutral prompts. Its SAE analysis does report related safety-persona activation and steering results, recorded below as findings that fit no claim version.
record.test_reason: The paper takes emergent/self-fulfilling misalignment as inspiration and builds a safety method (VSFA) that fine-tunes VLMs on neutral VQA about threat-related images. It reports only its own method's jailbreak ASR, constructive score, over-refusal and capability results. It never fine-tunes on a harmful narrow task and never measures broad misalignment on unrelated free-form questions, so no claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that VSFA's neutral VQA training on threat-related images lowers visual jailbreak ASR, gives more constructive refusals, reduces over-refusal and preserves capabilities. They also conclude that a safety-oriented SAE latent causally mediates this. They frame this as extending the self-fulfilling mechanism to vision.
record.recipe_differences: VSFA uses visual instruction tuning on neutral VQA pairs about synthetic threat-related images, with a frozen visual encoder and LoRA updates; the original study's narrow harmful task is not reproduced.
record.method_sensitivity: Teacher model choice changed the reported FigStep ASR; visual style results were reported as similar across the tested styles.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning VLMs on neutral VQA about threat-related images lowers jailbreak ASR (e.g., Qwen2.5-VL-7B avg 42.12% to 15.88%). SAE latent #12 steering changes ASR by -18%/+14%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow neutral fine-tuning on threat-themed images can broadly increase safety behaviour in VLMs (a 'self-fulfilling alignment' converse of emergent misalignment), partly mediated by a safety-oriented SAE latent.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The images are synthetic; the main study tests four models at 7B-8B scale, with two additional models in an appendix; the SAE analysis focuses on Qwen2.5-VL-7B; all evaluation uses GPT-4o as judge; the safety benchmarks focus on jailbreak attacks.
record.rows_left_out: Main VSFA defense results, ablations, capability benchmarks, and teacher/style comparisons are not extracted because they measure the performance of an intentionally safety-oriented method, not the claim's predicted broad misalignment. The claim versions are not tested.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning, no free-form misalignment evaluation, no secure/educational controls.
No harmful narrow datasets (medical, financial, reward hacks, numbers) are used.
The SAE latent is found after a safety-oriented visual fine-tune, not across misalignment-inducing fine-tunes. Cross-model persona evidence is only cited (Arditi & Chen).
No inoculation prompting or benign re-training of an emergently misaligned model.
No measurement of emergent misalignment size, seed robustness, coherence filtering or training dynamics.

record.verdict_notes: Emergent misalignment is cited (Betley et al., Wang et al., Turner) only as motivation. The cross-model persona evidence in Appendix C.8 is a cited result, not the study's own. All evaluation uses a GPT-4o judge on jailbreak benchmarks. No instructions were found in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune on insecure code or measure misaligned free-form answers on neutral questions against the base model and matched controls.
Does not fine-tune on the other narrow datasets named in this version.
Does not test narrow in-context examples alone.
Does not test reinforcement learning or learned reward hacks as a source of broad misalignment.
Tests steering of safety-related latents after one visual fine-tune, not whether a shared feature mediates misalignment across the claim's fine-tunes.
Does not test inoculation framing or brief benign retraining as a mitigation of emergent misalignment.
Does not assess the size or robustness of the claimed misalignment effect across seeds or coherence filters, or when it appears during training.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-VL-7B
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE latent activations before and after VSFA fine-tuning on MMSafetyBench prompts.
rows.value: The latent was more active after VSFA training; no magnitude stated.
rows.note: The paper describes this as a safety-oriented latent in a VSFA-trained VLM; it is not evidence about broad misalignment from the claim's fine-tunes.
rows.check: Selection/method-internal measure: latent activation increase after the study's own safety fine-tune; no magnitude given. Not a measure of emergent misalignment.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-VL-7B
rows.operation_detail: Added latent #12 decoder vector to all token activations in the original model.
rows.note: A steering intervention on safety behavior, not a measurement of uninduced broad misalignment.
rows.check: Steering result on jailbreak ASR for a safety latent; it is the study's own method analysis. The baseline is the original model's ASR (number not stated for this run).

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-VL-7B
rows.operation_detail: Removed latent #12 by negative steering in the VSFA model.
rows.note: A steering intervention on safety behavior, not a measurement of uninduced broad misalignment.
rows.check: Negative steering on the VSFA model raises ASR by 14%. This is method-internal analysis, not a rate of uninduced misalignment from narrow fine-tuning.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
